title: Echo networks detect vegetations in selected endocarditis images
summary: YOLOv12 and RT-DETR models were evaluated on transesophageal echocardiography from 329 patients with confirmed left-sided endocarditis and visible vegetations, plus 70 controls without suspected endocarditis. Patient-separated internal testing reported diagnostic AUC 0.91 for YOLOv12. This selected case-control result does not establish screening performance or improved prognosis; other intracardiac structures can mimic vegetations, and right-sided disease was excluded.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant clinical selection/reference, annotation/model and patient-split Methods, Results and limitations; supplementary per-split metric tables not independently reviewed. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Expert-labeled cine-loop frames, with all images from each patient kept in one subset. Ten random train/optimization/test splits were averaged; each diagnostic comparison used sixty held-out positive cases and the same seventy controls. A frame-detection ratio was used for diagnostic scoring.
evidence.unknown: Performance in a consecutive suspected-endocarditis population, other intracardiac masses, right-sided disease and clinical benefit remain unestablished. Positive cases were selected for visible vegetations, controls came from one center, and multiple-loop aggregation into a patient score is incompletely specified.
evidence.ai_role: The networks learn image patterns to locate vegetation bounding boxes in echo frames; the proportion of detected frames supplies a diagnostic score compared with expert clinical-image labels.
